This page computes the additional numbers quoted in the main text from the prepared student and dyad datasets. Its calculations include the all-dyad model needed for the quartile comparison, so no saved Table 1 is required.

**Sample and design.** Size of the sample, number of decisions per child and rounds per classroom.

```{r numbers-packages}
#| code-summary: "numbers-packages"
```


The data are reused if `analysis_dyads` and `analysis_students` are already in R. Otherwise, this step loads their CSV files from `data/generated/main/`, or builds them from the raw inputs on first use.

**Rank differences children actually meet.** The full range of the rank gap (from bottom to top of a classroom) occurs for only one pair per classroom. This block looks at a more common contrast: pairs between a child in the top quarter of the classroom ranking and one in the bottom quarter, and the Cooperation GAP that Table 1 predicts for them.

```{r numbers-quartiles}
#| code-summary: "numbers-quartiles"
#| output: false
```

```{r show-numbers-quartiles}
#| code-summary: "show-numbers-quartiles"
numbers[c("percent_top_vs_bottom_pairs", "predicted_coop_gap_top_to_bottom", "observed_coop_gap_top_to_bottom")]
```

**Filtered analysis.** The Table 1 model uses `coop_gap_filtered`, which is observed only when both directed transfers pass the filter. Figure 3C summarizes retained transfers within children instead; its filtered curve and these regressions use different aggregation rules.

```{r numbers-filtered}
#| code-summary: "numbers-filtered"
#| output: false
```

```{r show-numbers-filtered}
#| code-summary: "show-numbers-filtered"
rbind(all = filtered_all, non_friends = filtered_non, mutual = filtered_mut)
```

**One-sided friendships.** How often the exchanges fall in each region of Figure 3A.

```{r numbers-asymmetric}
#| code-summary: "numbers-asymmetric"
#| output: false
```

```{r show-numbers-asymmetric}
#| code-summary: "show-numbers-asymmetric"
numbers[c("percent_full_cooperation_asym", "percent_strongly_asymmetric_asym", "percent_blue_region_asym")]
```

**A rank read off the game.** Instead of nominations, rank can be computed from the token network itself (PageRank on who gives to whom). This block correlates that behavioral rank with the nomination-based Social Rank.

```{r numbers-behavioral-rank}
#| code-summary: "numbers-behavioral-rank"
#| output: false
```

```{r show-numbers-behavioral-rank}
#| code-summary: "show-numbers-behavioral-rank"
numbers[grepl("spearman", names(numbers))]
```

